sentences.text: The claimants in M.V.C.No.1175/2015 have filed this appeal challenging the judgment and award passed by the learned II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT VII, Vijayapura dated 31.03.2021 for enhancement of compensation.
2. The matter is listed for hearing on admission and with the consent of the learned counsel on both sides, the matter is taken up for final disposal.

3. Brief facts of the case of the petitioners/ appellants that on 16.04.2015 at about 10.30 a.m.,
deceased Bhimashankar Mallinath Mahamane was proceeding as pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.MH-13/AU-8899 and Amogsidda Basavanappa was riding the said motor cycle.
They were going from Hunnur towards Chappalgaon Village.
They met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the Car bearing Reg.No.MH-44/G-6100 by its driver, which was coming from opposite direction.
As a result of which, Bhimashankar NC: 2023:KHC-K:5431-DB sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries at the spot.
Claimants are wife and children of deceased Bhimashankar.

It is the further case of the clamant that the deceased was aged about 38 years and was working as Supervisor in Sai Constructon Engineers and Contractors, Solhapur and was earning salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.
All the claimants were depending upon his earnings.

With these reasons, the claimants have prayed to award compensation of Rs.22,75,000/-.
4.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the Insurer of the offended Car.
They have denied the case of the claimants.
They also denied that accident had taken placed due to rash and negligent driving by its driver.
On the contrary, they have contended that accident was caused due to negligence riding of the motor cycle by its rider and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
5. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues.
The claimants examined PW-1 and got marked Exs.P1 to P9.

The Respondent got marked Ex.R1.
7.
The Tribunal, on hearing both the sides and on appreciating the pleadings and evidence on record, awarded compensation of Rs.7,44,900/-.

8. The learned Advocate for appellants has submitted that the Tribunal has taken income of the deceased as Rs.5,500/- through claimants have submitted that the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month and Salary Certificate was produced at Ex.P9, that was not considered.

If claimants were unable to prove Ex.P9, then the Tribunal could have taken notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month, which is also taken while settling the dispute in the Lok-Adalath Sujata And Ors vs Asmitha Dhananjay Kokate And Anr on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116850389/
3 for the accident occurred in the year 2015.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further stated that the Tribunal has not added future prospects.
The deceased was aged below 40 years.
Therefore, 40% of the income needs to be added towards future prospects.
He has further submitted that the Tribunal has not awarded just NC: 2023:KHC-K:5431-DB compensation towards loss of consortium, which needs to be enhanced.
With these reasons, prayed to enhance the compensation.
9. The learned Advocate for Respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and submitted that it doest not call for any interference.

10. The following point emerges for our determination:
"Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
11.
The fact of accident and death of Bhimashankar in the said accident taken place on 16.04.2015 is not disputed.
The Tribunal, on appreciating the evidence on record held that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of Car by its driver and the same is not challenged by the respondents.
12. It is undisputed that age of the deceased was 38 years.
The Tribunal in the impugned judgment held that the claimant was unable to prove income of the deceased as NC: 2023:KHC-K:5431-DB Rs.25,000/- per month.

Therefore, notional income of deceased was taken as Rs.5,500/- per month,
which is seriously disputed by the claimants.
It is true that the claimants have not examined author of Ex.P9 and not able to prove Ex.P9.

While settling the dispute in Lok-Adalath pertaining to motor vehicle compensation cases, notional income of the victim of the accident of the year 2015 is considered as Rs.8,000/- per month, the same could be applied to the present case.
In the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS1, 40% of income of deceased must be added towards his future prospects since the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There were three dependants on the earnings of the deceased.
Therefore, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal expenses, i.e., Rs.3,733/-.
It is not in dispute that the multiplier applicable to the facts of this case is '15'.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency'
Income of deceased per month 8000 Add 40% of future prospects 3200 11,200 Less 1/3rd of personal expenses 3733

Total net income 7467X12X15 (multiplier)= Rs.13,44,060/-
12.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection.

It is held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra) and in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS2, Rs.40,000/- shall be awarded to each claimants towards loss of consortium.

entities.text: MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, there are three claimants.
Therefore, claimants are entitled for Rs.1,20,000/- towards loss of love and affection and consortium.

sentences.text: 4 13. The compensation awarded under the conventional heads of funeral expenses as well as loss of 2 (2018) 18 SCC 130 NC: 2023:KHC-K:5431-DB estate by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
It shall be inconsonance with the law laid down in the case of PRANAY SETHI.
Therefore, it needs to be re-calculated and Rs.15,000/- each is awarded under the said heads.

14. For the aforesaid reasons, the claimants are entitled for following amount of compensation:
 Sl.

No Particulars Amount  (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 13,44,060  2. Loss of consortium 1,20,000  3. Funeral expenses 15,000  4. Loss of estate 15,000  Total 14,94,060

The claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.7,49,160/-.
15.

For the aforesaid discussion, we answer the above point partly in the affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER
The Appeal is partly allowed with costs.

The impugned judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.1175/2015 by the II Additional - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5431-DB Senior Civil Judge and MACT VII, Vijayapura dated 31.03.2021 is modified as under:
a) The claimants are entitled for compensation of Rs.14,94,060/- (Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Ninety Four Thousand Sixty only) as against Rs.7,44,900/- awarded by the Tribunal and claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.7,49,160/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Forty Nine Thousand One Hundred and Sixty only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced amount from the date of the petition till its payment.
b) Respondent No.2 shall deposit the said enhanced amount within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this award.
c) The Tribunal's finding regarding apportionment, deposit and release are not disturbed.
